prompt.context: Our client, CD OutBev, is a major alcoholic beverage distributor. They have asked us to estimate the daily market size for alcoholic beverages on US domestic flights.
prompt.question: First, brainstorm a few ways we might approach this problem. Once we agree on an approach, work through the assumptions to size the market in terms of number of drinks and dollars per day.

clarifying_info.q: Should I focus on number of drinks, dollars, or both?
clarifying_info.a: We are looking for number of drinks and dollars, in that order.

clarifying_info.q: Should I work top-down or bottom-up?
clarifying_info.a: Either is fine — share your approach and we can align on one.

framework: Top-down approach: Start with total US domestic passengers per year, estimate % who purchase alcohol, derive daily figure
Bottom-up approach (preferred): Start with number of gates at one airport, build up to total daily flights, then estimate passengers and drinks purchased
Segment passengers by age to account for legal drinking age restrictions
Calculate total drinks purchased, then convert to dollar value using price per drink
If asked about investment, apply present value of a perpetuity formula

questions.prompt: How many domestic flights take place in the US per day?
questions.guidance: Candidate should build up from airports and gates. Strong answer: ~50 major airports x 50 gates = 2,500 gates; ~8 flights per gate per day (7am–11pm, one flight every ~2 hours) = 20,000 domestic flights per day.

math.setup: Major airports × gates per airport × flights per gate per day
steps: × 8 flights per gate per day = 20,000 domestic flights per day

questions.prompt: How many passengers are on those flights each day?
questions.guidance: Candidate should estimate average seats and a realistic load factor. Strong answer: 100 seats × 80% load factor = 80 passengers per flight × 20,000 flights = 1,600,000 passengers per day.

math.setup: Flights per day × seats per flight × load factor

questions.prompt: Now that we have our potential customer base, how would you further segment the market to arrive at total drinks purchased?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify that age is the right segmentation variable because of legal drinking age. Interviewer provides the following age breakdown and drink purchase rates. Key calculation: 2×80,000 + 2×192,000 + 1×56,000 = 600,000 drinks per day.

math.setup: Segment passengers by age → apply % who drink → apply drinks per drinker
steps: Age 20–40: 25% of 1.6M = 400,000 passengers; 20% drink = 80,000 drinkers; 2 drinks each → 160,000 drinks
Age 40–60: 40% of 1.6M = 640,000 passengers; 30% drink = 192,000 drinkers; 2 drinks each → 384,000 drinks
Age 60+: 25% of 1.6M = 400,000 passengers; 14% drink = 56,000 drinkers; 1 drink each → 56,000 drinks
math.answer: 600,000 drinks per day; $3.6M daily market size

questions.prompt: CD OutBev is considering purchasing exclusive rights to supply all alcoholic beverages on US domestic flights indefinitely for $2 billion. Given the market size we found and a 3% annual market growth rate, should they invest?
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize this as a present value of a perpetuity problem. Formula: PV = FCF / (r − g). Provide the formula if asked. Strong candidate knows it unprompted. Profit margin (50%) and cost of capital (13%) are provided when asked. PV = $630M / (0.13 − 0.03) = $6.3B > $2B → recommend investing.

math.setup: PV of growing perpetuity: PV = FCF / (r − g); FCF = daily market size × profit margin × days per year
steps: Daily revenue = $3,600,000; profit margin = 50% → daily FCF = $1,800,000
math.answer: PV ≈ $6.3B; since $6.3B > $2B, CD OutBev should invest

brainstorming.prompt: What are different approaches to sizing the daily market for alcoholic beverages on US domestic flights?

categories.name: Top-down
ideas: Start with total annual US domestic passengers (Bureau of Transportation Statistics data point ~900M/year)
Divide by 365 to get daily passengers
Estimate % who purchase alcohol to get drinks sold

categories.name: Bottom-up (preferred)
ideas: Count gates at a representative airport, extrapolate to all major airports
Estimate flights per gate per day using operating hours
Multiply by passengers per flight and load factor to get total passengers
Segment by age and purchase propensity to get drinks purchased

categories.name: Supply-side
ideas: Estimate number of airlines × aircraft in service × average drinks stocked per flight
Use airline catering data or SEC filings if available

recommendation: CD OutBev should purchase the exclusive rights for $2 billion
The present value of the opportunity is approximately $6.3 billion, more than three times the $2 billion asking price, indicating significant positive NPV
risks: Estimate relies on several assumptions (load factor, age distribution, purchase rates) that could be materially wrong
Regulatory changes or health trends could reduce alcohol consumption on flights
Exclusivity economics depend on ability to capture full market share and maintain margins
next_steps: Validate key assumptions (actual load factors, purchase rates) with airline data
Confirm cost of capital assumption and refine profit margin estimate
Assess contract terms — duration, exclusivity scope, price escalation clauses
